$comment: Job handlers registered in a composition root that nothing enqueues, so they have
never run. Read by scripts/check-job-producers.mjs, which fails on a new one.
A ratchet, not a mute button: an entry whose handler has gained a producer, or been
deleted, also fails the check with the line to remove. It can only shrink.
Nothing here is endorsed by being here. Both rows are features that read as finished
in two reviews -- the handler exists, it is wired, the code inside it is correct --
and have never executed. The fix is either the missing producer or deleting the
registration, and both are application decisions rather than CI ones.

known.why: Registered in packages/db/src/postgres-services.ts and packages/services-memory/src/index.ts. No caller anywhere enqueues it, so invites have never been expired by this path. InvitePort.expireOld exists and is called from the account-jobs timer in apps/rest wiring with a `.catch(() => 0)`, so the behaviour is not entirely absent -- but the job kind, its dedupe and its retry are dead, and the timer's swallowed error means nobody learns when it fails either. Delete this row when a producer exists, or when the registration goes.

Registered in both composition roots with no producer. Trash purging does happen, through the minute-ly setInterval in apps/rest/src/server.ts calling wiring.purgeTrash() directly, which is why nobody noticed: the feature works and the job does not. That timer is also the one that took the process down for want of a `.catch`. Moving the sweep onto this handler is the obvious fix and is a production change, not a CI one.
